messages:
mina: heads-up seeing a spike of ALB target deregisters in us-west-2 from edge pods after a scale-up. ~80 targets removed in 3m.
infra-bot: [ALB] 2026-03-15T10:12:34Z targets deregistered count=78 elb=redwood-edge-usw2
mike: interesting—any commonality? node? pod? az?
mina: all on nodes that got newly attached ENIs after autoscaler event. pods are gpu-inference pods w/ hostNetwork=false
selena: could be SNAT/egress translation weirdness: ALB healthchecks originate from LB, but reply path might leave via a different ENI so packet gets dropped or RST'd. also watch NAT port reuse.
mike: healthchecks are ALB -> pod ip:port. ALB expects 200 but connections often reset.
mina: grabbed netcat logs + tcpdump from one affected node. snippet below:
```
10:12:22.123 IP 10.0.3.45.52345 > 10.0.12.10.8080: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1
10:12:22.124 IP 10.0.12.10.8080 > 10.0.3.45.52345: RST
```
mike: RST from pod side suggests asymmetric conntrack or reply src IP differs from expected. maybe ip-masq-agent rewrote source then another ENI answer.
selena: did kube-proxy or any network daemon restart during the autoscale? kube-proxy logs show an iptables restore around 10:11:50 on the affected nodes.
al: I see evidence of ENI rotation: primary ENI detached/attached during the same window. replies from pods go out via a different route than ALB ingress => conntrack mismatch.
sre-oncall: what's conntrack usage? run `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `..._max`.
mina: on node-7: count=96000 max=100000. high but not saturated. ephemeral port reuse visible in conntrack dump.
mike: even without full exhaustion, ENI flip can cause active entries to map to the wrong device and RSTs.
selena: short-term mitigation ideas: preserve SNAT source across ENI swaps, move ALB target type to instance so LB hits node IP (then kube-proxy handles routing), or force pods to respond from expected IP?
mina: risky to change target type mid-traffic. planning: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes to let targets re-register on stable ENIs 2) roll kube-proxy config to avoid iptables restore churn 3) add alerting on ENI attach/detach coincident with ALB deregisters.
sre-oncall: agree. also add a runbook step: if deregisters spike > 30 in 5m and conntrack > 90% then suspend new autoscale actions.
infra-bot: [ALB] 2026-03-15T10:14:05Z targets registered count=60 elb=redwood-edge-usw2
mina: partial recovery after draining two nodes, but still seeing sporadic drops on one AZ.
selena: please attach tcpdumps and kube-proxy logs to the ticket. leaning toward evaluating instance-target mode for a narrow test.
mike: opened a small test cluster with instance-target ALB in us-west-2 staging to verify path consistency.
mina: opening INFRA-4221 with timeline, tcpdumps, conntrack dumps, and proposed mitigations. will update when we validate instance-target test. :link:
__notes: This thread is a single continuous Slack conversation string per agents.md. No title field included.
